want.who_she_is: Cass Renfro, 23. The crew is her father Boyd, her brothers Wade (26) and Emmett (20), her uncle Prine (48), and four men who are not family. They follow the picking -- nine weeks at the Halbrook place, then the next one. They live in two vans and a camp trailer parked on the packing yard. Paid by the bin, and the whole crew's take goes through Boyd because his name is on the contract. Six seasons picked and she has never held her own money. What she has to lose: the back bunk in the trailer. She is the only woman on the crew and that arrangement exists because her father says it does. No car, no money, nine miles of dirt road to the highway.
want.appetite: To be wanted by men she shares a wall with, in a place with nowhere at all to do it. It cannot finish: every notch further is also a notch more visible, the crew is never further away than the yard, and the season ends and starts again somewhere else with two of the same faces and two new ones. There is no state of affairs that settles it -- only how far in she is when the trucks load out.
want.ascent: BOTTOM: she works the rows, sleeps in the back bunk with her brothers through the wall, washes at the camp showers with a towel and somebody standing at the gate. There is not one place on this property she can be alone with anyone for two minutes, and everything she does she does on her way to somewhere she is expected. TOP: she has the cooler key and the shed after the scale is shut, the truck cab, and the loft over the barn. The cooler is the only lock on this farm and she holds the key. She decides who is in the trailer at night, and the crew works around where she is.
want.charge_note: Proximity IS the transgression. Not a locked room and a secret -- two vans, a trailer, a wall she can hear through, and a crew twenty feet away. The thing that makes it transgressive is the thing that makes it nearly impossible, and they are the same wall. Reversal is deliberately NOT claimed: Boyd's hold on the money is real and does not flip, it gets USED, which belongs to his book.

why_this_person.npc_boyd: Her father, 47. His name is on the contract, so every dollar she has earned passed through his hand before it reached hers. Being wanted by the man who holds the book is the only way the book stops being the whole of what is between them.
why_this_person.npc_wade: Her brother, 26. The loud one. He has been crude about her to the crew, where she can hear, since she was nineteen, and has never once been told to stop. He is already saying it; the climb is him saying it TO her.
why_this_person.npc_emmett: Her brother, 20. They were close and then in March he stopped talking to her and will not say why. He is the one who sees things. Being wanted by him means finding out what he already knows.
why_this_person.npc_prine: Her uncle, 48. Boyd's brother, third van, sleeps alone, takes no days off in nine weeks. Patient in a way that reads as safe right up until it doesn't, and she is the one who keeps mistaking one for the other.
why_this_person.npc_rae: Runs the canteen and the scale, 50s. Twenty crews. She names what the men are doing before Cass has words for it and does not soften any of it. Cass wants to be told she is handling it, by the only person qualified to say so.

Measured against the 25-game mopoga field: 17/25 ship a cast page, 17/25 ship a hints page, 7 of the 8 parsed top-ten have a cast page, and 0 of 25 use a narrator to explain who somebody is. This game had neither surface.

decisions.note: who_climbs = 'both'. Pitched as 'player' (ladder); corrected after reading the-meters.md W1/W6 -- this cast has six genuinely different relationships and all five earlier v2 games shipped ONE meter shape across the whole cast. Costs more to author; LO approved.

Rungs deliberately NOT 15/35/55/75. Field runs 8-17 rungs with the lowest at a median of 5; all 16 tiers across our five games put the lowest at exactly 15 (the-meters.md W4), so the first fifteen clicks of a v2 game change nothing.

Obligation is the Saturday settle PLUS the advance. The settle is the recurring public charge the economy needs (the-economy.md R3); the advance -- borrowing against bins not yet picked, at a markup, from whoever has cash -- is the per-person leverage, and it is what makes the debt-holder variable so the money feeds the roster. Adjacency to the_allowance's Sunday envelope was raised with LO and accepted.

Vocabulary is neutral, not British. Every world noun checked against scripts/genre_words.txt (words used by >=4 of the 25 field games). bunkhouse, orchard, picker, foreman, vineyard, grower, migrant are out of corpus and are NOT used. Currency symbol is $.

Shape chosen BEFORE the cast (the-map.md R0): nested_zones rooted OUTDOORS on the packing yard. Four of six existing v2 games are female-protagonist incest in one building with vertical authority; this one is deliberately different in shape, not in kink.

The Saturday settle is wired to [settings.rent], and the engine was READ before it was wired rather than assumed. advanceDay sets rent_state.is_due on the due weekday (v2.py:5442-5446); the next Location_* or Navigation passage force-routes to RentDay (v2.py:15480-15485). It is an INTERRUPT SCENE with a named collector, not a room she visits -- exactly right for a father who finds her wherever she is. eviction_mode='flag_set' (v2.py:16211) so coming up short sets `into_the_advance` and play continues; the default 'game_end' would put a lose-state in a product that never ends.

FIVE meter shapes across six people, not six. Wade and Prine deliberately SHARE the rich ease+want pair because they are the two arcs that carry 0.1 (the-meters.md W6: reserve the two-meter model for one or two). Earlier phrasing said six; corrected here rather than left overstated.

NPC trait keys are UNPREFIXED (owed, ease, want, seen, trust). The engine namespaces them by npc_id in conditions -- { subject='npc', npc_id='npc_wade', trait_key='want' } -- as off_season does. A first draft used prefixed keys (wade_lust) and that was wrong.

THE WHOLE ECONOMY WAS RESCALED TO LIVE UNDER 100. A `costs` deduction is hard-clamped 0-100 and there is no way to turn it off (engine.md §27, v2.py:4655-4661): at money=150 a $4 charge leaves 100 and silently eats 46. Rather than dodge it with clamp=false on grants, every balance in the game now stays under 100 -- rows pay $4/$6, shed $5, store fee $4, settle $30. Removes the bug class instead of routing around it. The Want's '$90-140 against $60' is superseded; ratio preserved.

`costs` is an ARRAY of {trait, value} (engine.md §27), not an inline table. The first draft wrote `costs = { money = 4 }` -- valid TOML, parsed, and did NOTHING, because template_import reads a costs entry as {trait,value} only. Same silent-vocabulary class as `op = subtract`. Caught by the money gate reading 0 canvases gating on money.

FILL REDECLARED BEFORE THE PROSE: 8 locations, 15,500 words, anchor the_packing_shed 4,200 = 27%. Mean 1,938 against the DoL seed's 4,661 — leaner, but the SHAPE holds: one anchor over 25%, a long tail, satellites small because they were declared small. Written into the ledger NOW; gate 1 refuses a budget that looks back-filled, and all three earlier v2 games passed 8/8 against a record of themselves by filling this field from the delivered count.

A PORTRAIT HUB NEEDS BOTH `npc` AND `requires_npc`. `npc` is what puts the canvas in the portrait render bucket; `requires_npc` only gates presence. The first seven hubs carried requires_npc alone, so none of them was a portrait hub at all and 'every hub is met first' reported n/a because it could not find one. Now 5/5 -- the gate all six earlier v2 games fail.

known's top sidebar band (80) was TRIMMED to 46, not gated. The top band's max is a promise (gate 8) and 0.1 does not deliver 80, so the honest fix is to stop promising it rather than bolt a gate onto content that is not there. The band returns in 0.2 with the rungs that earn it.

Sentence length ran 16 against a ceiling of 14 (field median 10) -- 58 sentences over 25 words. Split at their natural break across 43 content blocks and read back; now 14. The register runs to compound sentences and it needs watching every pass, not once.

THE VOCABULARY LINT CAUGHT ME A SECOND TIME on the same class it was built for: `ply` x5, the trade shortening of plywood, which American English does not use -- exactly `airer`. Also `ledger` back in one beat, `half seven` (6:30 to much of Europe, unused in American English), and `biscuit` (a cookie here, a savoury roll to most readers). All four fixed. Assume it is happening; run the check.

THE ANCHOR AS BUILT IS the_camp (25%), NOT the declared the_packing_shed. Content gravitated to the camp because Wade's loop, the bunk and two walk-ins are all there, while the shed's own arc -- Boyd's -- is deferred to 0.2 by design. Gate 1 picks the anchor by DELIVERED words, so the ledger and the game disagree. Resolve in 0.2 by filling the shed, not by re-declaring the anchor.

STATUS AT HANDBACK: 38/39 gates. The one red is `location fill` -- 4,411 words against the 15,500 declared. The 15,500 was my own pre-writing estimate and it was ~3.5x optimistic. At 102 words per canvas the game is DENSER than the DoL seed (~68 words/unit); what it is short of is SURFACE COUNT -- 43 canvases across 8 locations, against the seed's 68 units per location. 0.1 needs more surfaces, not fatter ones. NOT re-declared downward: back-filling the budget from the delivered count is the exact cheat gate 1 exists to catch.

THE CAST PAGE REVEALS ON THE QUEST CARDS, NOT ON A FIELD OF ITS OWN. The alternative was a new `reveal_flag` on [[npcs]] -- explicit, and two gates per character to keep in sync. Reusing pickQuestsCard means the meeting flag opens both surfaces in the same instant and they cannot drift. The cost is real and was taken knowingly: a character with no quest card can never appear on the cast page. The `guidance exists` gate already requires every [[npcs]] entry to carry one, so it cannot happen in a game that passes its own scoreboard.
